Title: August 6, 2026 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
Overview: The council heard extensive open comment and staff presentations, then voted on five ordinances for the November 3, 2026 ballot. It unanimously referred the firefighter collective bargaining charter amendment (8761), the recreation and safety bond (8758, amended to name a lap pool), and the debt limit charter amendment (8762), and referred the residential vacancy excise tax (8759) by a 7-1 vote. The downtown development authority measure (8763) failed 4-4, and the council then directed staff to scope community engagement; the meeting ended by approving the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update conditions and amendments.

Topic1.Title: Open Comment
Topic1.Summary: Residents spoke on the Fort Chambers interpretive design, Sand Creek memorialization, Spruce Pool and South Boulder Rec Center, a shelter bathroom sanitation issue, HOA costs in permanently affordable homes, and Middle East policy. Staff responded that they would follow up with Right Relationship Boulder, Spruce Pool would close for renovations after Labor Day, and the shelter issue was being addressed with shelter leadership and public health. Council members raised tribal consultation timing, CU Boulder coordination, and the city's investment portfolio.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda and Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic2.Summary: After reconvening at 6:30 p.m., the council passed the consent agenda items 3A through 3C by voice vote. Three outside city utility permit requests on Cherryville Road, Frying Pan Road, and Cottonwood Drive were not called up for discussion.

Topic3.Title: Recreation and Safety Bond Presentation and Debate
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented a proposed 400 million dollar general obligation bond to fund replacing the South Boulder Rec Center, renovating North Boulder Rec Center and the West Senior Center, and building a public safety and 911 dispatch facility, along with fire station and municipal building work. Staff said the bond would address a backlog of facilities needs that developed over decades and cited a 6.5 million dollar projected 2027 general fund gap. Residents and council members pressed for binding ballot language guaranteeing the South Boulder Rec Center's core amenities, such as a lap pool and gym.

Topic4.Title: Debt Limit Charter Amendment
Topic4.Summary: Staff explained that ordinance 8762 would change the city charter debt limit calculation from assessed value to actual value, bringing Boulder in line with other Boulder County communities and state statute. Council discussed the change as part of its long-term financial strategy. The council then approved the measure unanimously for the November ballot.

Topic5.Title: Residential Vacancy Excise Tax
Topic5.Summary: Ordinance 8759 would impose an excise tax on homes occupied 183 days or fewer per year, starting January 1, 2028, at 4,000 dollars per unit with annual CPI adjustments up to a maximum of 7,000 dollars per unit. Supporters said it would encourage long-term rentals and help housing affordability, and staff said an implementing ordinance would address exemptions. Council member Nicole Speer opposed, arguing a fee would be a better approach, and the council referred it to the ballot 7-1.

Topic6.Title: Firefighter Collective Bargaining Charter Amendment
Topic6.Summary: Ordinance 8761 would add a new charter section guaranteeing full-time fire department employees the right to bargain collectively, along with changes to the impasse procedure. The Boulder Association of Firefighters and city leadership reached agreement on the language, avoiding a petition effort. The council adopted the ordinance unanimously for the November ballot.

Topic7.Title: Downtown Development Authority Presentation and Council Questions
Topic7.Summary: Staff presented the proposed downtown development authority covering downtown and University Hill, with tax increment financing projections, a draft letter of intent, and council oversight through appointments and budget approval. Staff said the DDA would be a separate entity, that roughly 2,200 qualified electors in the district would vote, and that the bond and DDA projections were separate from the city's citywide forecast. Council questions addressed sales tax base years, Sundance Film Festival timing, precedents from other Colorado DDAs, and whether water supply was included in long-term projections.

Topic8.Title: Public Hearing on Ballot Measures
Topic8.Summary: More than 60 residents spoke, with strong opposition and support on the DDA, the rec center bond's lack of binding amenity language, and the vacancy tax. Speakers included library trustees requesting a board seat and an IGA, Downtown Boulder Partnership and Chamber representatives supporting the DDA, and Sierra Club and open space advocates raising concerns about dedicated tax revenue. Several speakers also opposed or supported the collective bargaining measure and questioned the bond's debt obligations.

Topic9.Title: Council Votes on Ballot Measures
Topic9.Summary: The council unanimously adopted ordinance 8761 for firefighter collective bargaining and then approved ordinance 8758 unanimously after adding a lap pool to the South Boulder Rec Center language. Ordinance 8759 passed 7-1 with Council Member Spear opposed, and ordinance 8762 passed unanimously. Ordinance 8763 to form the DDA failed 4-4, and council gave staff direction to scope next steps and community engagement by a 6-0 show of hands.

Topic10.Title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan Update
Topic10.Summary: Staff presented remaining conditions of approval and recommended amendments from the planning board, county commissioners, and county planning commission. Council accepted staff's recommendation to approve the conditions and amendments, including the county's revised municipal airport policy, the removal of the history section, and the rural lands designation for area 2. A proposal to restore near-transit language for neighborhood one housing failed a straw poll, and all three motions passed unanimously.
